answer: Imagine a mesa settlement where citizenship is earned by seasons, not fees. A newcomer may rest at the harbor hostel, but full haven rights come only from time-released chores: a commit-reveal beacon announces each task at a random hour with a short completion window. Because schedules are secret and every alias needs a live responder at unpredictable moments, capital cannot buy tenure; an attacker must staff each synthetic identity around the clock for months, and one missed window resets its ladder. Wall-clock attendance becomes scarce, non-transferable collateral.
